- [00:00:00] 📊 Data Science vs Data Analytics

- Data science and data analytics are often confused but serve different purposes.
- Data science encompasses tasks like data mining, machine learning model training, and AI deployment.
- Data analytics is a specialized field within data science focusing on querying, interpreting, and visualizing datasets.

- [00:01:47] 🔄 Data Science Lifecycle

- The data science lifecycle consists of seven phases: problem identification, data mining, data cleaning, data exploration analysis, feature engineering, predictive modeling, and data visualization.
- It's an iterative process where hypotheses are formed and tested with data.
- Essential skills for data scientists include proficiency in Python, R, big data platforms (like Hadoop or Apache Spark), and SQL.

- [00:03:30] 📈 Types of Data Analytics

- Data analytics involves various types: predictive, prescriptive, diagnostic, and descriptive analytics.
- Predictive analytics forecasts trends and outcomes, while prescriptive analytics provides decision recommendations.
- Diagnostic analytics identifies causes of events, and descriptive analytics evaluates data qualities and quantities.

- [00:05:16] 🧮 Skills for Data Analysts

- Data analysts focus on interpreting existing data to derive actionable insights.
- Skills required include analytical thinking, programming (especially in statistical tools), database familiarity, and data visualization.
- Unlike data scientists, data analysts are less involved in creating new algorithms but rather in interpreting and applying data findings effectively.

Troubleshooting:

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
For Non-US Students: Set Your 'Locale for Import'
- This step is crucial for anyone working outside of the United States. Our course files use US formatting for dates (e.g., Month/Day/Year) and numbers (e.g., salary data). This setting ensures Power BI reads the data correctly.

Note for US students: Your setting is likely correct already, so you can probably skip this step!

🗺 How to check:
Go to File > Options and settings > Options.
Under the CURRENT FILE section, click on Regional Settings.
If you are outside the US, ensure the Locale for import dropdown is set to English (United States).
Click OK.

-----------------------------------------------------------
🔐 Fix Power BI’s “Login After Every Click” Bug
If Power BI keeps prompting you to sign in after every single action, this is a known issue caused by Preview Features + downloaded .pbix files.

🛠 Fix #1 (Try This First ✅)
⚙ Disable Problematic Preview Features
🔓 Open any course or blank .pbix file
📂 Navigate: File → Options and settings → Options
🧪 Click: Preview Features (left sidebar)

Uncheck ALL of these:
🚫 Save to OneDrive and SharePoint
🚫 Share to OneDrive and SharePoint
🚫 Translytical task flows (if visible)
🔄 Restart Power BI Desktop

🧠 Why This Works
These preview features try to auto-connect your local file to Microsoft's cloud services, which forces Power BI to re-authenticate constantly. Turning them off puts it back in true desktop mode.

🧯 Backup Fixes (Only If Fix #1 Doesn't Work)

🛠 Fix #2 — Sign In to Power BI Desktop
The simplest fallback. Power BI's popup behavior is suppressed when you're signed in.
📂 Go to: File → Sign In
Sign in with any Microsoft account (a free personal one works fine)
🔄 Restart Power BI Desktop

🛠 Fix #3 — Registry Fix (Windows Only, No Sign-In Required)
If you'd rather not sign in at all, this disables the popup at the system level.
- Press Win + R, type regedit, hit Enter
- Navigate to: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Microsoft Power BI Desktop (create the folders if they don't exist)
- Right-click → New → DWORD (32-bit) Value
- Name it ShowLeadGenDialog, set the value to 0
🔄 Restart Power BI Desktop
📝 If that path doesn't work, try the alternate documented path: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Microsoft Power BI Desktop with the same ShowLeadGenDialog = 0 setting.

🛠 Fix #4 — Disable Integrated Windows Authentication (Corporate/VM Users)
If you're on a work network or running Power BI inside a virtual machine:
- Open the Start menu and search for Internet Options
- Click the Advanced tab
- Under the Security section, uncheck Enable Integrated Windows Authentication
🔄 Restart Power BI Desktop
⚠ Note: This is a more advanced change that can affect other Windows apps relying on Integrated Windows Authentication, so only try this if the earlier fixes haven't worked.

🍎 Fix #5 — Mac / Parallels Users Only
📂 Go to: File → Options → Security
✅ Check: Use updated sign-in experience
🔄 Restart Power BI Desktop
